claim.pdf_says: (operand-1<sub>1</sub> + operand-1<sub>2</sub> + ... + operand-1<sub>n</sub>)  [general rule 1; subscripts 1, 2, n printed as subscripts]
claim.why_it_matters: The subscripts are flattened onto the baseline, so the text reads 'operand-11' and 'operand-12' (apparently operands numbered eleven and twelve) instead of the first and second instances of operand-1. The surrounding prose ('the values of operand-1 are ...') shows what is meant, but the expression as written is wrong.

verdict.reasoning: Rendered PDF page 491 (printed page 467, §2014:14.9.2.3 ADD general rules) shows GR1's expression as '(operand-1 + operand-1 + ... + operand-1)' with clearly lowered subscript glyphs 1, 2 and n after each 'operand-1'. The markdown (page-491.md line 17) reads '(operand-11 + operand-12 + ... + operand-1n)' with the subscripts flattened to the baseline and no subscript markup, so the tokens read as different operand names (operand-11, operand-12). The claim quotes both sources accurately. The same defect also occurs in GR2 (markdown line 29: '(operand-11 + operand-12 + ... + operand-1n + operand-2)' vs printed subscripts), which the claim does not mention. GR3 '(operand-1 + operand-2)' has no subscripts and is correctly transcribed. The meaning is recoverable from the following 'where the values of operand-1 are ...' prose, so the impact is on readability of the expression rather than on the rule's semantics; the subscript loss is nevertheless a genuine content defect, not mere furniture or reflow.
verdict.corrected_description: On page 491 (§2014:14.9.2.3 GR1 and GR2 of the ADD statement), the markdown flattens the printed subscripts 1, 2, n on operand-1 to the baseline in both arithmetic expressions: GR1 '(operand-11 + operand-12 + ... + operand-1n)' and GR2 '(operand-11 + operand-12 + ... + operand-1n + operand-2)' should read operand-1 subscript 1, subscript 2, ..., subscript n. Meaning is recoverable from the surrounding prose, so the severity is closer to editorial than normative.
